one_liner: Alpha C++20 synchronous logger (console, file, rotating targets) whose own crude benchmark beats spdlog's single-threaded sinks.
what_it_does: A home-grown synchronous logging framework with ConsoleTarget, FileTarget and RotatingTarget classes, each a self-contained logger with its own pattern, level, flush policy and optional mutex (multi-threading support is off by default). The API is Trace/Info/Debug/Warn/Error/Fatal with {}-style format strings on the target object; it is not spdlog-compatible (no registry, no sinks, different pattern flags such as %k and %N). Formatting goes through a bundled ArgFormatter, fmtlib or MSVC <format>.
how_it_is_fast: The file targets format straight into a std::vector<char> owned by the target and only issue a raw _write/write call when that buffer reaches pageSize (4 MB on Win64, 2 MB on Win32, 64 KB elsewhere), so syscalls are rare compared with spdlog's FILE*-based basic_file_sink. The pattern is pre-compiled once into a format string, the time breakdown is cached and refreshed only when the second changes, and the level check is a plain enum compare before any work.
when_to_use: Single-threaded Windows/MSVC program that logs large volumes of text to one file and can tolerate up to several MB of unwritten log on a crash
Learning or experimenting with a small, readable logger codebase built on C++20 concepts and jthread
Writing a home-grown sink and wanting a reference for buffer-then-bulk-write file output
when_not_to_use: Any production use: the README calls it an alpha learning project and the last commit was 2023-03-25

Linux or macOS builds: FileHelper.cpp defines a 'Write' macro for non-Windows while the code calls WRITE, uses Windows-only _O_WRONLY/_O_BINARY flags and the MSVC STL internal path::_Remove_filename_and_separator, and CI is a single msvc.yml workflow
Latency-critical or multi-threaded hot paths: logging is synchronous on the calling thread; async front ends such as Quill, fmtlog, NanoLog or XTR are an order of magnitude cheaper per call
Crash-safe logging: with the default never-flush policy up to a full page buffer (4 MB on Win64) is lost if the process dies
Code that already depends on spdlog's API, sinks, registry or pattern flags

integration.dependencies: none by default (bundled ArgFormatter); optional fmtlib or MSVC <format>; CMake with CPM for benchmarks
integration.min_toolchain: C++20; MSVC is the only toolchain exercised by CI (msvc.yml); <format> backend needs MSVC
integration.platforms: Windows (MSVC); Linux/macOS code paths present but the non-Windows file I/O macros do not match the call sites
integration.thread_safety: Opt-in per target via EnableMultiThreadingSupport (mutex around format and write); off by default

gotchas: The console benchmark rows measure nothing but the disabled-level check: both Serenity and spdlog console loggers were set to level off, so 5.656 ns vs 10.837 ns is a branch, not output

The current bench/src/Benchmark.cpp runs 2,000,000 iterations and passes a std::string_view (its comment says string_view is faster than the C string), whereas the README table says 1,000,000 iterations of a C-style string, so the published numbers predate the checked-in harness

The file speedup largely compares buffer sizes: Serenity holds up to 4 MB (Win64) in a vector before one _write, versus spdlog's stdio-buffered fwrite; front-erasing the vector after each page write is a memmove
FileHelper::CloseImpl tests close() != 1, so close errors are never reported
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Rarely: lwlog and fmtlog also beat spdlog with maintained code and published harnesses, and Quill, XTR or PlatformLab NanoLog are far cheaper on the hot path via async back ends. Choose Serenity only as a small synchronous single-threaded Windows file logger to study or vendor.
verified_claims_summary: First-party README table dated 05Jul22: one thread logging a 400-byte string, Serenity FileTarget 215.981 ns vs spdlog basic_file_sink_st 1125.735 ns (about 5.2x), RotatingTarget 627.968 vs spdlog rotating_file_sink_st 2919.572 ns (about 4.6x), console 5.656 vs 10.837 ns (about 1.9x, but with both loggers at level off) (ratios derived from page data); compiler, flags, CPU and spdlog version not stated, and the harness was apparently built with MSVC on Windows.
status_note: Abandoned alpha (last commit 2023-03-25, 3 stars) under MIT; copyable in principle but effectively Windows/MSVC-only and not production-ready.
